seo.title: Bhutan Culture and Family Tour | Adventure Access
seo.description: Five to seven days in Bhutan: Thimphu, Punakha Dzong over Dochu La, a Paro farmhouse with hot stone baths, and the Tiger's Nest hike. From $3,300.

hero.imageAlt: Punakha Dzong across the river below forested hills

intro.label: The Journey
intro.heading: A Week in the Dragon Kingdom
paragraphs: Bhutan is a place of old forests, clear rivers, snow-capped peaks and warm, tropical valleys. This Buddhist kingdom is one of the least visited countries in the world, yet it has some of the best hiking, biking, rafting and cultural immersion in the Himalaya.
This one-week itinerary pairs Bhutan's history, culture and food with activities chosen to fit your appetite for adventure.

dayTypes.label: How the Days Work
dayTypes.heading: Culture First, Then Choose
dayTypes.lede: The first days are paced for the altitude. Punakha is where you choose activities, or add time if you want more.

cards.title: Capital days
cards.body: Days 1–2: the drive from Paro to Thimphu, then a walking day with a dzong, a cultural museum and the Takin Preserve.

cards.title: Punakha
cards.body: Days 3–4: over Dochu La to Punakha Dzong, with hiking, biking, rafting or fishing to choose from.

cards.title: Paro
cards.body: Days 5–7: a farmhouse stay with hot stone baths, the Tiger's Nest hike, then your flight home.

chapters.label: The Journey in Chapters
chapters.heading: From the Capital to the Tiger's Nest

groups.title: Thimphu — Into the Capital (7,656 ft)

image.alt: Prayer flags above the Thimphu valley

prose: Approaching Bhutan is like nothing else. The Himalaya fill the horizon, and your first Bhutanese hosts are on the plane, since only the national airlines fly in and out. Paro is just the port of entry for now; you will see the best of it at the end.

days.label: Day 1
days.text: Land in Paro (7,200 ft), a quick meal, then about an hour's drive to Thimphu. Check in and take it easy to adjust to the altitude, then dinner with the group and a full orientation from your guides.

days.label: Day 2
days.text: A walking day in the capital at an acclimatizing pace: a dzong, a cultural museum and the Takin Preserve, for a first look at Bhutan's Buddhist culture, history and wildlife.

groups.title: Punakha — Dochu La and the Great Dzong
prose: Punakha is an adventurer's dream: hiking, biking, rafting, fishing, fortresses and old myths. Its riverside dzong was built in 1637, saw the coronation of the first king in 1907, and was the capital until 1955.

days.label: Days 3–4
days.text: Over Dochu La, with views of Bhutan's great peaks from the top, then down to Punakha. Wander the dzong while your guide explains its many roles, and choose from several activities, or go further with one. This is the place to extend the trip.

groups.title: Paro — Farmhouse and the Tiger's Nest

image.alt: The Tiger's Nest monastery on its cliff

prose: Back to where it began. A family farmhouse, some dating back seven or more generations, is home in Paro, with homegrown food and a hot stone bath. The Tiger's Nest can only be reached on foot, and the hike is the best way to end any trip to Bhutan.

days.label: Days 5–6
days.text: Walk Paro's streets, try Bhutan's homegrown coffee and shop for something to remember the trip by. Hike to the Tiger's Nest, then reward yourself with another hot stone bath.

days.label: Day 7
days.text: Your guide takes you to Paro airport for your flight home.

highlights.title: The Tiger's Nest
highlights.body: One of Bhutan's most iconic places, reachable only on foot. The hike combines activity, culture and mountainside forest in one day.

highlights.title: Punakha Dzong
highlights.body: Built in 1637, site of the first king's coronation in 1907 and Bhutan's capital until 1955.

highlights.title: A Day in the Capital
highlights.body: A dzong, a cultural museum and the Takin Preserve: Bhutan's Buddhist culture, history and wildlife in one walking day.

goodToKnow.label: Good to Know
goodToKnow.heading: Before You Go
goodToKnow.lede: A few things that shape how this trip runs.

cards.title: Getting there
cards.body: Only Bhutan's national airlines fly into Paro, the country's one international airport. Flights to and from Bhutan are not included.

cards.title: Altitude
cards.body: Paro sits at 7,200 feet and Thimphu at 7,656 feet. The first days are paced to help you adjust.

cards.title: Your guides
cards.body: Professional English-speaking guides travel with you, with English-speaking guides for each activity.

cards.title: Hot stone baths
cards.body: A Bhutanese tradition common in Paro's farmhouses, and a highlight for any trip to Bhutan.

stays.label: Where You'll Stay
stays.heading: Hotels and a Farmhouse
paragraphs: Our preferred packages use 3–4 star hotels in Bhutan. In Paro you stay with a family in a farmhouse, some dating back seven or more generations. Farmhouses are not rated like hotels, but every guest names them as a highlight.

included: Professional English-speaking guides and activity guides
Activities as listed in your itinerary
Accommodations: 3–4 star hotels and a farmhouse stay
All ground transportation by private vehicle
excluded: Alcohol (we strongly encourage little or none while acclimatizing)
Tips for guides (we will explain local tipping customs)
Personal clothing and equipment (we send a packing list)
